situation:
You are the recruitment coordinator for RIVER BEND UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT, a public school district serving eleven schools and about six thousand students. The assistant superintendent for human resources (judge) has asked you to recommend how the district should change the way it hires classroom teachers, and how the change should be explained to the families and staff who take part in it.

The district has hired the same way for two decades. Applicants teach a sample lesson in front of a panel of teachers and parents, and the panel's recommendation decides the offer. Families are told about the panel at enrollment, and the district points to it as the reason its new teachers stay. The process takes five weeks from application to offer.

CEDAR LINE ACADEMIES, a charter network that opened two campuses inside district boundaries last year, interviews and makes an offer in four days. This spring the district lost nineteen of its top candidates to that network, most of them before the panel had met. Enrollment has followed the teachers, and three of the district's schools opened the year with long-term substitutes in place of teachers.

One route is to move to a single interview day and an offer within forty-eight hours. That closes candidates, but it removes the panel, and the district would be setting aside the guarantee it makes to families at enrollment and the voice its teachers have in who joins them. Another route keeps the panel and sends a conditional offer in the first week, which the district would have to withdraw whenever the panel later disagrees.

The assistant superintendent (judge) wants your recommendation on which route the district takes, and what the district tells applicants and panel members about it. You will present your recommendation to the assistant superintendent (judge) in the district office. The assistant superintendent (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the assistant superintendent (judge) will thank you for your work.
